objective: cost(p) = sum over i, j of a[i][j] * b[p(i)][p(j)], with a the first and b the second matrix of the .dat file and p a 1-based permutation.

qaplib.text: R.E. Burkard, S.E. Karisch, F. Rendl. QAPLIB – A Quadratic Assignment Problem Library. Journal of Global Optimization 10:391–403, 1997. Instance and solution tables at Lehigh University, last updated April 2012.

goncalves2017.text: A.D. Gonçalves, A.A. Pessoa, C. Bentes, R. Farias, L.M.A. Drummond. A graphics processing unit algorithm to solve the quadratic assignment problem using level-2 reformulation-linearization technique. INFORMS Journal on Computing 29(4):676–687, 2017.

fujii2021.text: K. Fujii, N. Ito, S. Kim, M. Kojima, Y. Shinano, K.-C. Toh. Solving challenging large scale QAPs. ZIB-Report 21-02, arXiv:2101.09629, 2021.

shylo2017.text: V.P. Shylo, repeated iterated tabu search on the SCIT-4 supercomputer. Reported on the QAPLIB mirror at Polytechnique Montréal, November 2017 (archived copy).

misevicius2019.text: A. Misevičius. Letter: New best known solution for the most difficult QAP instance “tai100a”. Memetic Computing 11:331–332, 2019.

sergienko2024.text: I. Sergienko, V. Shylo, V. Roshchyn, P. Shylo, D. Boyarchuk, V. Moroz. Algorithm portfolios for solving the quadratic assignment problem. Cybernetics and Computer Technologies 2024(3):25–33 (in Ukrainian). The paper prints the permutation.

sergienko2026.text: I.V. Sergienko, V.P. Shylo, V.O. Roshchyn, D.O. Boyarchuk. Applying algorithm unions to specific classes of Boolean programming problems. Cybernetics and Systems Analysis 62(4):578–587, 2026. Reports a further improvement on tai100a; the value could not be checked yet and is not listed until its permutation is available.

mittelmann2026.text: H.D. Mittelmann. Improved QAPLIB lower bounds using BBCPOP and NewtBracket. Web page dated 26 August 2026.

quadi.text: QUADI (T. Baylis, quadi.dev), as listed by H.D. Mittelmann on 26 August 2026.

enumeration.text: Proved optimal for this page by complete enumeration of all 10! permutations (3 November 2026). These two instances are in the QAPLIB data archive but not in its table.

mittelmann2026log.text: H.D. Mittelmann, NewtBracket log for this instance (2026): the valid bound in the log, rounded up to the next integer as the log's summary line does. QAPLIB data are integers, so the optimum is an integer; the table on his page shows the bound rounded down.

fujii2025.text: K. Fujii, S. Kim, M. Kojima, H.D. Mittelmann, Y. Shinano. An exceptionally difficult binary quadratic optimization problem with symmetry: a challenge for the largest unsolved QAP instance tai256c. Optimization Letters 19(6):1075–1097, 2025. Proves the lower bound 44,200,000 by branch and bound; the higher bound listed here (QUADI) has not been published in a paper.

bur.description: Typewriter keyboard design: typing times of a stenotypist and letter-pair frequencies in several languages.

chr.description: One matrix is the adjacency matrix of a weighted tree, the other that of a complete graph.

els.description: Hospital layout: distances between 19 facilities and the flow of patients between them.

esc.description: Testing of self-testable sequential circuits, minimising the extra hardware.

had.authors: S.W. Hadley, F. Rendl and H. Wolkowicz (1992)
had.description: Manhattan distances of a cellular complex in the plane; flows drawn uniformly from [1, n].

kra.description: Real data used to plan the Klinikum Regensburg hospital in Germany.

lipa.description: Generated asymmetric instances with known optimal solutions.

nug.authors: C.E. Nugent, T.E. Vollmann and J. Ruml (1968)
nug.description: Manhattan distances of rectangular grids; the most used QAPLIB instances.

ste.description: Backboard wiring with Manhattan, squared Euclidean and Euclidean distances.

tai.description: taiXXa uniformly random; taiXXb asymmetric, random but structured like real-life instances; taiXXc from the generation of grey patterns.
